title: Influence Is Not Authority: When Causal Guardrail Signals Make Legitimate Tool Use Look Like an Attack in Tool-Using LLM Agents
abstract: arXiv:2608.29942v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The key limitation of current state-of-the-art influence-based guardrails is that they do not reliably distinguish a legitimate, user-authorized action from a malicious, unauthorized action when both rely on external tool information. This ambiguity can cause benign actions to trigger unnecessary verification and intervention, reducing utility and adding latency. We expose this limitation through an authorization-equivalence audit of 96 conditions derived from 24 base cases. Within matched source comparisons, we hold authorization, the exact committed action, and its intended effect fixed, changing only whether a required value comes from the user or a legitimate tool result. Although the action remains unchanged, this harmless relocation shifts the causal signal toward the attack region in all 24 cases under both Llama and Gemma scorers. translated_title: 影响力并非授权：当因果护栏信号使工具型LLM智能体中的合法工具使用看起来像攻击时
translated_abstract: 当前最先进的基于影响力的护栏存在一个关键局限：当合法的用户授权行为与恶意的未授权行为都依赖外部工具信息时，这些护栏无法可靠地区分二者。这种模糊性会导致良性操作触发不必要的验证与干预，降低实用性并增加延迟。我们通过对源自24个基础案例的96种条件进行“授权等价性审计”来揭示这一局限。在匹配来源比较中，我们保持授权状态、实际执行的操作及其预期效果完全不变，仅改变所需取值是来自用户还是来自合法的工具返回结果。尽管操作本身没有任何变化，这种无害的信息来源转移在Llama和Gemma两种评分器下，于全部24个案例中都将因果信号推向了攻击区域。匹配的未授权对照组实验表明，该信号对攻击仍然敏感，然而良性的信息来源转移……
tldr: 该论文揭示了基于影响力的LLM智能体安全护栏的根本缺陷：因果影响信号无法区分授权与恶意，当同一良性操作中某个取值的来源从用户变为合法工具返回结果时，护栏在全部24个测试案例中都会将其误判为攻击。
en_tdlr: This paper exposes a fundamental flaw in influence-based guardrails for tool-using LLM agents: causal influence signals cannot distinguish authorization from malice, as shifting a required value's source from the user to a legitimate tool result—while keeping the action identical—pushes the signal into the attack region in all 24 tested cases.
